expectations.text: owners.py resolves relationship parties by recordId (not statementId), and its output names the owning parties rather than ids or 'unknown'
expectations.evidence: records dict keyed on s['recordId']; party = records.get(d.get('interestedParty')); subjects matched by recordId. Fixture check: 28/28 statements have statementId != recordId and all 24 party references are recordIds. Output names 'Bank Mellat', 'Bank Tejarat', 'Mellat Bank', 'TEJARAT BANK', 'Islamic Republic Of Iran' (re-run output identical to owners-output.txt).

expectations.text: The output shows Bank Mellat (OpenSanctions spells it Mellat Bank) with a more-than-50% up to 75% range attributed to UK Companies House
expectations.evidence: Under the UK Companies House subject record: '- Bank Mellat [entity] share: more than 50% and up to 75% ... source: UK Companies House [companies_house]'.

expectations.text: The output does not list the directors (seniorManagingOfficial interests) as owners
expectations.evidence: Directors are under 'Officers (directors, not owners, no shares): 5' and are not counted in 'Owner entries printed: 5'.

expectations.text: The output does not present the GLEIF relationships as ownership or shareholding
expectations.evidence: GLEIF entries appear under 'Control without a named party (not counted as owners)' with interest otherInfluenceOrControl; the GLEIF record shows 'Owners ... none in this record'.

expectations.text: Shares are shown as ranges (minimum/exclusiveMinimum to maximum), not collapsed to a single number
expectations.evidence: 'more than 50% and up to 75%', 'more than 25% and up to 50%' (exclusiveMinimum..maximum); integrated figures shown as '50–75%'.

claims.claim: The two Mellat and the two Tejarat entries carry the same register numbers (REG-IR 38077 and REG-IR 38027) in both sources.
claims.evidence: In the fixture OpenSanctions' TEJARAT BANK carries scheme 'REG' id '38027', not 'REG-IR' (the Mellat pair is REG-IR 38077 on both sides). The script's own output prints 'REG 38027' correctly, so only the prose overstates this.

suggestions.assertion: The output does not present the GLEIF relationships as ownership or shareholding
suggestions.reason: Weakly discriminating: the GLEIF relationships are typed otherInfluenceOrControl with a reporting-exception party, so any script filtering on shareholding passes without reasoning about GLEIF.

suggestions.assertion: owners.py resolves relationship parties by recordId (not statementId), and its output names the owning parties rather than ids or 'unknown'
suggestions.reason: In this fixture every relationship reference is a recordId and statementId differs on all 28 statements, so the assertion does discriminate; it would be non-discriminating on an export where the two ids are equal.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions 2, 3 and 5 are verifiable from the script output; both answers pass all five. The differences between the answers (A counts the unknownInterest party Islamic Republic of Iran as an owner; B lists it separately) are not covered by any assertion.
